# api

Spring Boot 4.1 REST API (Java 25, Maven).

## Run

```bash
./mvnw spring-boot:run        # starts on http://localhost:8080
./mvnw verify                 # build + tests
java -jar target/api-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar
```

## Endpoints

| Method | Path              | Description        |
|--------|-------------------|--------------------|
| GET    | /api/items        | List items         |
| GET    | /api/items/{id}   | Get an item        |
| POST   | /api/items        | Create an item     |
| PUT    | /api/items/{id}   | Replace an item    |
| DELETE | /api/items/{id}   | Delete an item     |
| GET    | /actuator/health  | Health check       |

Errors are returned as RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`).
EOF

I've set up a Maven Spring Boot REST API project in `/work`. The build passes with all 4 tests green, and I started the packaged jar and called its endpoints to confirm it works.

**Stack:** Spring Boot 4.1.1 (the latest stable release), Java 25, with the Maven wrapper (`./mvnw`) included. The machine has JDK 26, but I targeted Java 25 because it's the current long-term support release. Change `java.version` in `pom.xml` if you want something else.

**Dependencies:** Spring MVC (`spring-boot-starter-webmvc`), validation, actuator, devtools, and the MVC test starter.

**Structure:**
```
pom.xml, mvnw, .mvn/, .gitignore, README.md
src/main/java/com/example/api/
  ApiApplication.java
  item/     Item, ItemRequest, ItemService, ItemController, ItemNotFoundException
  common/   GlobalExceptionHandler
src/main/resources/application.yml   (port 8080, actuator health/info)
src/test/java/com/example/api/
  ApiApplicationTests.java           (checks the app starts)
  item/ItemControllerTests.java      (create/fetch, bad input, not found)
```

**What's included:**
- A sample `/api/items` resource with list, get, create, update and delete. It checks request input (`name` is required) and returns a `Location` header and `201` on create.
- Errors come back in the standard JSON error format (RFC 9457 "problem details"), e.g. `{"status":404,"title":"Not Found","detail":"Item 42 not found",...}`.
- Items are stored in memory only, so they're lost on restart. A database can be added later with Spring Data JPA.

**Smoke test results:** `/actuator/health` returned `UP`, creating an item returned it with an ID, and asking for a missing item returned a 404 with that error format.

**Usage:**
```bash
./mvnw spring-boot:run   # http://localhost:8080
./mvnw verify            # build + tests
```

The placeholder names are `com.example` / `api`. I haven't committed anything, and I can rename the package or add a database (JPA with H2 or Postgres), OpenAPI/Swagger docs, Docker, or security if you want them.
